core.title: Assert the exact telemetry URN in telemetry tests
core.given: A test is a telemetry test: it claims telemetry URNs in its binding header(s), or is identified as one by a telemetry URN segment in its path or by colocation with the telemetry emitter.
core.when: Writing, changing or checking that test, including edits to its binding header(s) or to a claimed item's identity.
core.then: Every telemetry URN claimed in the test's binding header appears verbatim in the test's code as an assertion string (a string literal that takes part in an assertion, not an unused literal); a telemetry test with no such header asserts at least one concrete telemetry URN. Once generated contracts ship, the item's contract identifier satisfies this the same way.
prefer: Name the telemetry item in the assertion itself: assert that the emitter was called with the item's exact URN string and its payload.
avoid: Asserting the mocked emitter was called with any argument.
Asserting a URN prefix or a captured-anything matcher.
Relying on the URN in the binding header or any comment — comments do not assert.
A quoted URN present in code but never used in an assertion.
unless: The repository has not adopted this rule family — the rule is inert until adoption, like every rule in the family.
core.why: An any-call assertion proves emission, not that the planned item fired; renames and copy-paste drift hide there. Exact URNs keep assertion and plan from silently diverging.
evidence: For each telemetry URN claimed in the test's binding header(s), the same URN occurs verbatim as a quoted string in the comment-masked test source, and that string takes part in an assertion (not an unused literal).
For a telemetry test with no binding header (identified by URN segment or colocation), at least one concrete telemetry URN string is asserted in comment-masked code.
The stack's telemetry-test check reports no finding for this rule, and a reviewer confirms the matching strings are used in assertions.
verification: Claimed URNs are the URNs listed in the test's telemetry binding header(s) (binding syntax from the profile). Which files count as test files comes from the profile's role assignment for the test roles (roles.assignment and each test role's kinds); the stack does not differentiate test kinds for this rule. Applicability is determined by the test file's classification (binding header / URN segment / colocation), never by task wording; task terms are a non-gating discovery hint only.
Mask comments (comment syntax from the profile) before searching; header and comment occurrences never satisfy the rule.
The match must be the concrete URN verbatim inside a string literal: not a prefix, not a captured-anything matcher, not a comment.

Mechanical check: each claimed URN is found as a quoted string in comment-masked source. The obligation is that this string takes part in an assertion (used directly or nested in an asserted value); literal presence alone is the detector's approximation.

Telemetry tests identified only by URN segment or colocation must assert at least one concrete telemetry URN string in code (any concrete telemetry URN of the profile's telemetry URN space satisfies this, not only one example shape).
When generated contracts ship, a contract identifier for the item satisfies the check the same way as the URN literal (equally acceptable, not preferred).
The rule is inert until the repository adopts the telemetry rule family.
Severity 3, disposition strict: every finding fails the check; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: telemetry test: telemetry binding header present, telemetry URN segment in path, or colocated with the telemetry emitter

fires: A test with a telemetry binding header whose code only asserts that the emitter was called, with any argument.
A telemetry test whose claimed URN appears only in the binding header or another comment, not in an assertion string in code.
A telemetry test whose claimed URN appears only as an unused string literal (e.g. a constant never used in any assertion).
A telemetry test identified only by URN segment or colocation that asserts no concrete telemetry URN.
A telemetry test asserting a URN prefix or a captured-anything matcher instead of the full URN.
A task that renames a telemetry item or edits a test's telemetry binding header without touching assertions, leaving claimed and asserted URNs out of sync.
doesNotFire: A non-telemetry test file (no telemetry binding header, no telemetry URN segment, not colocated with the telemetry emitter).
A repository that has not adopted the telemetry rule family (rule inert).
A telemetry test whose assertions contain every claimed URN verbatim as a string literal (whether passed directly or nested in an asserted value).
Once generated contracts ship, a test asserting the generated contract identifier for the item.

profileRequirements.meaning: How a file is assigned to a test role for this rule: in this stack the test runner's complete test-file classification assigns a file to every test role alike (the stack does not differentiate unit, acceptance and e2e test files), and a file that is not a test file is out of scope. The classification is the runner's own recognition, not a suffix list — the note's example suffix is illustrative only — and it covers test files in both of the stack's languages (TypeScript and JavaScript test files alike).
profileRequirements.bunValue: "Bun test files (e.g. *.test.ts)." — the runner's complete test-file classification; *.test.ts is an example, not the recognition rule, and JavaScript test files (e.g. *.test.js) are equally covered

profileRequirements.bunValue: "Bun test files (e.g. *.test.ts)" — the runner's whole test-file classification (example suffix not exhaustive; JavaScript tests included)

profileRequirements.meaning: Line-comment syntax of the stack's source files, used to mask comments and binding headers before searching for asserted URNs.

The URN space of telemetry items: every concrete telemetry URN, of any kind. Claimed URNs of any shape within this space must be matched verbatim, and a headerless telemetry test may satisfy the rule with any concrete telemetry URN from this space; the event form is one example, not the exclusive shape.
profileRequirements.bunValue: any concrete `telemetry:` URN — the `telemetry:`-prefixed URN space generally (e.g. `telemetry:event:be:example:item-accepted`); claimed URNs and headerless assertions are not limited to the event form

profileRequirements.meaning: The syntax by which a test file declares (binds itself to) the telemetry URNs it claims; claimed URNs of any shape within the telemetry URN space are binding.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `// Telemetry:` header comment(s) listing the claimed telemetry URNs (e.g. `// Telemetry: telemetry:event:...`)

proposedKeys.meaning: The URN space of telemetry items: every concrete telemetry URN, of any kind. Claimed URNs of any shape must be matched verbatim, and a headerless test may satisfy the rule with any concrete telemetry URN from this space; no single kind (e.g. event) is exhaustive.
proposedKeys.bunValue: any concrete `telemetry:` URN — the `telemetry:`-prefixed URN space generally (e.g. `telemetry:event:be:example:item-accepted`); claimed URNs and headerless assertions are not limited to the event form
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn group's artifact params (component, acceptance, smoke_acceptance, train, wmbt, wagon, feature, journey) include no telemetry artifact, and no other key describes a telemetry item's URN space.

proposedKeys.meaning: The syntax by which a test file declares (binds itself to) the telemetry URNs it claims, of any shape within the telemetry URN space.
proposedKeys.bunValue: `// Telemetry:` header comment(s) listing the claimed telemetry URNs (e.g. `// Telemetry: telemetry:event:...`)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.binding.<artifact> exists only for the enumerated artifacts; telemetry is not among the params, and no other binding key fits a test's claimed telemetry URNs.

neutralityNotes: The telemetry URN space and the binding-header syntax have no key in the closed vocabulary, so urn.telemetry and urn.binding.telemetry are proposed (group urn) and also listed in profileRequirements; urn.telemetry denotes every concrete telemetry URN — the event form telemetry:event:... is retained only as an example, so claimed non-event URNs and headerless tests asserting any concrete telemetry URN keep Bun's exact treatment. Test-file recognition is profile data through role assignment, not suffixes: Bun declares no suffix/name-pattern rule of its own, so the runner's complete test-file classification is recorded in roles.assignment and the three test roles' kinds entries (the note's `*.test.ts` is an example, and JavaScript test files are equally covered by that same classification); no suffix key is used. The Bun language activation fact (typescript/javascript) stays with the realization as the family's scoping device; no profile key carries a test-language-gate or test-recognition meaning beyond its documented sense. Comment masking (// -> idiom.comment_marker) is profile-sourced. Kept as bunOnly: the language activation fact, the validator id bun_telemetry_test, and the concrete assertion idiom in prefer[0] (the core states the pattern at role level; bun.json stays the worked example). 'String literal', 'captured-anything matcher', 'comment masking' and 'mocked emitter' are treated as near-universal testing concepts and kept in core wording. The 'generated contracts ship' provision names no stack and is kept verbatim. Severity 3 / strict disposition are per-rule enforcement and live in core verification, not the profile.
